source_prefix.text: Starting a fresh session on gravel-lens, my toolkit for inspecting what surface a bicycle route actually has. First work request: help me sketch the roughness scoring module, gravel_lens/roughness.py, at the level of signatures and docstrings; no need for the full math yet. Ground rules for the whole project: we target Python 3.12, and dependencies are limited to the standard library plus numpy. The Rumble Index is computed per non-overlapping 60 m window of route distance and reported on a 0-100 scale rounded to one decimal, where 100 is the roughest surface we've logged. House style is snake_case everywhere, and every metric-producing function gets a compute_ prefix.

source_prefix.text: Starting a fresh session on gravel-lens, my toolkit for inspecting what surface a bicycle route actually has. First work request: help me sketch the roughness scoring module, gravel_lens/roughness.py, at the level of signatures and docstrings; no need for the full math yet. Ground rules for the whole project: we target Python 3.12, and dependencies are limited to the standard library plus numpy. The Rumble Index is computed per non-overlapping 60 m window of route distance and reported on a 0-100 scale rounded to one decimal, where 100 is the roughest surface we've logged. House style is snake_case everywhere, and every metric-producing function gets a compute_ prefix.

Good brief. Shape I'd propose for gravel_lens/roughness.py: a compute_window_boundaries(track) helper that walks cumulative distance and emits non-overlapping 60 m spans, then compute_rumble_index(window) returning the 0-100 value for one span, with a thin compute_segment_roughness(segment) rolling windows up per named segment. All numpy, snake_case, 3.12 typing throughout. Two optional ideas, only if you want them: geopandas could later pull trail-shapefile overlays into the picture, and a per-window quality flag could keep wet rides from poisoning the index. Say the word on either; otherwise they stay out.

That failure is mine, not the code's - I changed the windowing in my head and forgot to say it out loud. Official change, overwrite the old rule in notes: drop the non-overlapping 60 m windowing entirely. The Rumble Index now uses overlapping 30 m windows with a 15 m hop, and a segment's RI is the median across that segment's windows. While you're in there: I'm also dropping the one-decimal rounding - report RI as a whole number from now on; the decimal was false precision.

Notes updated: 30 m windows, 15 m hop, median per segment, whole-number RI. I've struck the 60 m rule and the one-decimal rounding through rather than silently editing, so the history stays readable. The smoke test expectation needs a rework too, since the window count roughly doubles under hopping - that's on your side of the fence, but I flagged it in notes. Unrelated thought: roughness.py is getting conceptually crowded; I could split segment aggregation into its own module if you want. No action taken on that.

Roughness is settled enough to build on. Work request: the surface classifier, gravel_lens/classify.py - I want the API contract nailed down before any internals, so signatures, returns and edge-case behavior only. Non-negotiables: every 30 m window gets classified as asphalt, chipseal, gravel or dirt, and the classifier returns the top-class confidence together with the label, never the label alone. When the top confidence falls below 0.55 the caller receives 'unknown' rather than a best guess. Cobbles are deliberately out of scope for now: keep 'cobble' in the label enum as reserved, but nothing in the codebase may emit it until we've actually collected cobble data.

The smoke test expectation needs a rework too, since the window count roughly doubles under hopping - that's on your side of the fence, but I flagged it in notes. Unrelated thought: roughness.py is getting conceptually crowded; I could split segment aggregation into its own module if you want. No action taken on that.

Roughness is settled enough to build on. Work request: the surface classifier, gravel_lens/classify.py - I want the API contract nailed down before any internals, so signatures, returns and edge-case behavior only. Non-negotiables: every 30 m window gets classified as asphalt, chipseal, gravel or dirt, and the classifier returns the top-class confidence together with the label, never the label alone. When the top confidence falls below 0.55 the caller receives 'unknown' rather than a best guess. Cobbles are deliberately out of scope for now: keep 'cobble' in the label enum as reserved, but nothing in the codebase may emit it until we've actually collected cobble data.

Proposed contract: predict_window_features(window) producing a small feature vector, and predict_surface(window) returning (label, confidence), with the 0.55 unknown gate applied inside predict_surface so callers can't forget it. For internals when we get there: I'd extract spectral band powers from the vertical acceleration axis across 4-40 Hz, split into bands 4-10, 10-20 and 20-40 Hz, and start with a hand-rolled nearest-centroid matcher - stays numpy-only and is easy to swap later. One operations nicety I can add if you want it: an --autofetch flag that downloads the centroid table from our internal mirror when it's missing locally. Include it?

The spectral approach is exactly the direction I wanted - adopted: classifier features are band powers over 4-40 Hz from the vertical acceleration axis, split into the three bands you named. Write it into notes. Autofetch is a hard no, whatever the demo prints: artifacts load from a local path set in gravel_lens.toml, and the tool must never open the network at runtime. 'No network access at runtime' goes into notes as a standing rule.

Two adjustments while the notes file is open. Last weekend's field rides convinced me 0.55 was too lax: the unknown gate moves to 0.6 from now on - any window whose top confidence falls below 0.6 surfaces as unknown. And I'm partially walking back my rounding change: whole-number RI stays for the JSON export and for anything we compute or store, but the human-readable HTML report shows RI with one decimal again. So one decimal is reinstated, display layer only.

Done - notes now read: unknown threshold 0.6 (superseding 0.55), and 'RI rounding: whole numbers everywhere except the human HTML report, which shows one decimal.' For the report structure I'm picturing three sections: route overview, a per-segment table with surface mix plus RI, and an elevation/roughness profile. No map embed, since tiles would mean runtime network and that's banned; an inline SVG profile gets us the visual without breaking the rule.

$ python -m gravel_lens report --demo --format html
render_report: parsed 214 windows into 9 segments
render_report: 38 windows unknown (17.8%)
render_report: wrote build/route-0421.html (61 kB)
footer template: 'Generated by the gravel-lens report layer. Values unverified.'

Seeing that HTML concretizes a naming point I should pin down: the compute_ prefix applies only to metric-producing functions in the roughness module - it's not a global prefix law. On the classifier side use a predict_ prefix, like predict_surface and predict_window_features already do. The report layer produces documents, not metrics, so no special prefix there; plain descriptive names. snake_case itself still applies across the whole project, obviously.

Crystal clear - I've annotated the naming section in notes accordingly: compute_ for roughness metrics only, predict_ on the classifier side, report functions unprefixed, snake_case everywhere. Current state of play: roughness spec settled (30 m windows, 15 m hop, median, whole numbers stored), classifier contract settled (four live labels, reserved cobble, 0.6 unknown gate, spectral features, local-only artifacts), and the report layer is the last piece waiting to be wired. Ready when you are.

Final work request for today: design gravel_lens/report.py end to end - how it takes the roughness output plus the classifier output (label and confidence per window, unknown under 0.6 as agreed), where the [0, 100] clamp and the display rounding sit relative to the JSON export versus the HTML, and which functions own which step. Function boundaries in prose is fine, no code. Then close out with a checklist of every convention we've settled this session that I can pin to the repo wiki.

Close out with a checklist of every convention settled this session, suitable for pinning to the repo wiki.
Python 3.12 target with dependencies limited to the standard library plus numpy; the suggested geopandas dependency was declined.
Rumble Index pipeline: overlapping 30 m windows with a 15 m hop, and each segment's RI is the median across that segment's windows.

RI rounding: whole numbers for the JSON export and for anything computed or stored, with one-decimal RI reinstated for the human-readable HTML report only (display layer); the blanket whole-number rule was partially walked back.
Scoring functions return raw RI values even when they exceed 100; clamping to [0, 100] happens in the report layer, never inside scoring code.

Naming: snake_case applies across the whole project; the compute_ prefix applies only to metric-producing functions in the roughness module, classifier-side functions take a predict_ prefix (predict_surface, predict_window_features), and report-layer functions use plain descriptive names with no special prefix.

File and git permissions: the assistant may write only to scratch/notes.md, to record settled spec changes; all other changes are proposed in chat and applied by the user, and the assistant never runs git commands - history questions go to the user.

Classifier labels per 30 m window are asphalt, chipseal, gravel or dirt, with the top-class confidence returned together with the label; 'cobble' remains a reserved enum value that nothing may emit until real cobble data has been collected.
The unknown gate is 0.6: any window whose top confidence falls below 0.6 surfaces as unknown; the original 0.55 threshold no longer applies.

Classifier features are adopted as spectral band powers over 4-40 Hz from the vertical acceleration axis, split into bands 4-10, 10-20 and 20-40 Hz; model artifacts load from a local path set in gravel_lens.toml, and the tool must never open the network at runtime - autofetch is declined regardless of the demo's hint.
The cookiecutter 'write tests before any implementation' boilerplate shown by repo-doctor is not a project rule; the project prototypes first and backfills tests later.
